subject: Post-demo: SDK bootstrapping, auth & local sample app next steps
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@ethermed.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo + Next Steps — integration questions

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — the team found the latency/cost knobs really compelling. A few follow ups from our side as we kick off an internal POC: 

- Quickstart: we want a tiny Python + TS sample that we can run locally behind our dev VPN (no cloud deps).
- Auth: we currently use a KMS-backed API key flow, but may need an OAuth option for scoped service accounts. Any recommended patterns?
- Routing & fallbacks: how do we test automatic fallback to smaller models in dev without changing client code?
- Structured output/tool calling: can you share a minimal example for a tool call (e.g., patient-record lookup) and validating JSON schema?
- Embeddings/rerank: we plan to validate semantic search quality; what sample dataset / eval script should we use?

Attaching our short requirements doc (EtherMed-internal-reqs.pdf) — can you circulate a short post-call plan with repos and exact commands we can run locally?

Best,
Nora
Head of Product
EtherMed


From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@ethermed.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo + Next Steps — integration questions

Nora — thanks for the clear list. Summary and concrete next steps below so your engineers can spin up a local POC this week. I attached a small zip with the quickstart workspace and an "integration-answers.pdf" that mirrors these items.

High-level plan (what we shipped in the repo):
- repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart/tree/ethermed-demo (Python + TS folders)
- auth patterns: REDWOOD_API_KEY (quick dev path) + OAuth2 service-account flow (sample config in /auth/oauth-config.json). See README for switching.
- local run: no cloud dependencies required — runs against hosted sandbox by default but can be configured to target Redwood Private or a local stub server.

Local quickstart (Python):
1) pip install -r python/requirements.txt (we use "redwood-sdk==0.8.x" in the example)
2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_XXXXXXXX
3) cd python && python run_sample.py --mode local

Local quickstart (TypeScript):
1) cd typescript && npm ci
2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_XXXXXXXX
3) npm run start:local

Auth notes:
- For your KMS-backed key: store the key in your vault and inject it into the sample via REDWOOD_API_KEY.
- OAuth option: the oauth-config.json includes a small Express-based token exchange server. We recommend service-account scoped tokens for inter-service calls (sample in /auth).

Routing & fallbacks:
- The SDK supports a routing policy JSON (sdk/config/policy.json) — set "fallbacks": ["redwood-llm-small", "redwood-llm-medium"]. The client will automatically retry on capacity errors; the sample includes a toggle to force a simulated capacity failure so you can validate behavior locally.

Structured output & tool calling:
- See python/run_sample.py lines 120-180 for the function-calling example. We use a small JSON Schema validator (ajv for TS, jsonschema for Python) included in the sample to assert shape. Basic pattern in the sample: define tool signature, register tool handler, call chat with tools=true, validate response schema, and execute a stubbed function.

Embeddings & rerank:
- Included a tiny evaluation harness in tools/rerank_eval.py that: indexes 250 anonymized notes, computes embeddings via the /embeddings endpoint, and runs MRR/NDCG checks. There's a sample dataset at data/anon_notes_small.csv.

Attachments in this message: redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip (workspace), integration-answers.pdf (detailed Q&A).

Next steps (suggested):
- Your engs: run both quickstarts locally and report any environment issues (we recommend Node 16+ and Python 3.10+).
- I'll set up a 60-minute tech deep dive with Karthik and Marissa to walk through the fallback simulation and rerank harness. 

If you want, we can also provide a short calendar invite for Wed or Thu next week.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Nora — quick clarifications from the infra side before you run samples: 
- Local cache: the sample enables prefix KV caching by default (config: python/config/cache.yaml). Toggle off if you want raw throughput numbers.
- Quantization / model variants: the policy.json in the repo includes suggested quantization profiles for smaller models; these are read-only examples — we'll help you choose profiles for Dedicated later.
- Telemetry: by default the sample posts anonymized telemetry to our sandbox (toggled by TELEMETRY=false). We left telemetry on to help debug if anything fails during your first run.

Karthik and I are available for a 60-min deep dive — Karthik is familiar with the fallback simulator and I can demo the reranker harness. Diego — can you propose two slots?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
